newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia debt crisis possible by end'98 - dep minister.
newsitem.headline: Russia debt crisis possible by end'98 - dep minister.

text.p: Russia could be heading for a debt crisis by the end of 1998 because its debt servicing costs are higher than the rate of economic growth, deputy finance minister Oleg Vyugin said on Wednesday.
"Economic growth is generally absent, and yields on (government) securities are high," he told a meeting of financiers.
GDP was six percent lower in the first 11 months of this year than in the same period of 1995 but the government is forecasting two percent output growth in 1997.
The interest rate on an issue of 140-day GKO discount Treasury bills at auction on Wednesday was 39.96 percent.

"The government is moving towards a debt crisis, that is towards a situation where internal savings are not enough to cover internal debt. There is no such crisis today, but we can calculate that by December 1998 we may be able to speak of a debt crisis in Russia," Vyugin said.
Russia was not threatened by the amount of its debt but by the high interest rates, he said.
As long as interest rates outstripped economic growth, the government would be unable to establish a buffer of reserves which would allow it to control treasury bill rates, he said.

"Experience shows that the availability of modest financial reserves in regard to work on financial markets allows one quickly to decrease interest rates and, on the other hand, absence of reserves allows market participants to force up interest rates, even if they are excessively high."

He said Russia needed to increase its reserves but was threatened by the lack of revenue from companies who would not or could not pay their debts. Tax collection has been a continuing problem for Russia in 1996.
"Companies do not fulfil their obligations to their workers, do not fulfil their obligations to the federal budget, and do not fulfil their obligations to the regional budgets," he said.
Central bank head Sergei Dubinin forecast on Wednesday the yield on governemnt securities would be between 17 and 19 percent by the end of 1997.
The State Statistics Committee said there were 233.22 trillion roubles by nominal value of outstanding GKO treasury bills and OFZ bonds on December 15.
